```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# The models have no between-replicate variability, so rxode2's note that a
# multi-subject solve has no omega is expected and is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}
```

# Model and source

Zhang 2019 is an in-vitro pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic integration study of
**doxycycline** against *Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae* strain ATCC25934, the agent of
porcine enzootic pneumonia. It has two quantitative pharmacodynamic layers -- a
sigmoid Emax kill rate fitted to static time-kill curves, and an inhibitory
sigmoid Emax fitted to PK/PD indices from a dynamic (dilution) apparatus that
reproduces porcine plasma doxycycline PK. The package carries one file per
fitted relationship.

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3389/fphar.2019.01088>

```{r models}
mods <- c(
  "Zhang_2019_doxycycline_killrate",
  "Zhang_2019_doxycycline_aucmic",
  "Zhang_2019_doxycycline_cmaxmic"
)
for (m in mods) {
  cat("##", m, "\n")
  cat(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(m))$description, "\n\n")
}
```

| Model file | Paper component | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Zhang_2019_doxycycline_killrate` | Sigmoid Emax kill rate composed with the dynamic-apparatus PK | Table 1 (row 12-48 h) + Materials and Methods, Description of the in vitro dynamic model |
| `Zhang_2019_doxycycline_aucmic` | Inhibitory sigmoid Emax on the AUC24h/MIC index | Table 2, AUC24h/MIC column |
| `Zhang_2019_doxycycline_cmaxmic` | Inhibitory sigmoid Emax on the Cmax/MIC index | Table 2, Cmax/MIC column |

```{r citation}
cat(rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Zhang_2019_doxycycline_killrate"))$reference)
```

# Population

All work is in vitro. *M. hyopneumoniae* standard strain ATCC25934 (Chinese
Veterinary Microorganism Culture Collection Center) was grown at 37 C and 5% CO2
in artificial medium base with 20% pig serum, cysteine and NADH. The doxycycline
MIC by broth microdilution was **0.125 ug/mL** (Results, Minimum inhibitory
concentration).

* **Static time-kill:** constant doxycycline concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6,
  8, 16, 32 and 64 times MIC, starting inoculum about 10^6 CFU/mL, counted at 0, 1,
  3, 6, 9, 12, 24, 36 and 48 h; at least three replicates on different days.
* **Dynamic apparatus:** a 210 mL absorption chamber feeding a central chamber of
  300 mL medium that holds a 10 mL dialysis tube with a 10^7 CFU/mL culture;
  peristaltic pumps at 0.58 mL/min. Eight regimens labelled 1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10,
  15, 20 and 30 mg/kg body weight were dosed into the absorption chamber once
  daily for 3 days, in triplicate.

The same information is available from each model's `population` metadata.

```{r constants}
MIC <- 0.125 # ug/mL, Zhang 2019 Results, Minimum inhibitory concentration
regimens <- c(1, 2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 20, 30) # mg/kg labels of the dynamic study
# Zhang 2019 Results (PK/PD modeling and analysis): reduction in log10 CFU/mL
# over the whole experiment for each regimen.
paper_reduction <- c(0.16, 1.29, 1.75, 2.94, 3.35, 3.91, 4.35, 5.77)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Kill-rate equation `E = Emax * C^N / (EC50^N + C^N)` | -- | Materials and Methods, Static time-kill curves fitting and analysis |
| `lemax` (kill rate) | log(0.06) 1/h | Table 1, row 12-48 h |
| `lec50` (kill rate) | log(0.78) ug/mL | Table 1, row 12-48 h |
| `lhill` (kill rate) | log(2.98) | Table 1, row 12-48 h |
| `lka` | log(log(2)/4.15) 1/h | Description of the in vitro dynamic model (absorption half-life 4.15 h) |
| `lkel` | log(log(2)/5.9) 1/h | Description of the in vitro dynamic model (elimination 5.9 h) |
| `lvc` | log(300) mL | Description of the in vitro dynamic model (300 mL central chamber) |
| `log10_cfu0` | 7 | Exposure to dynamic antibiotic concentrations (10^7 CFU/mL inoculum) |
| Index equation `E = Emax - (Emax - E0) * Ce^N / (EC50^N + Ce^N)` | -- | Materials and Methods, Intergration and modeling of PK/PD |
| `e0` (AUC / Cmax) | -3e-05 / -5e-05 | Table 2, row 'E max' (the paper's label for the control change) |
| `emax` (AUC / Cmax) | -2.13 / -3.14 | Table 2, row 'E 0' (the paper's label for the maximum effect) |
| `lec50` (AUC / Cmax) | log(179) h / log(21) | Table 2, row EC50 |
| `lhill` (AUC / Cmax) | log(1.38) / log(1.01) | Table 2, row Hill's slope |
| `mic` | 0.125 ug/mL | Results, Minimum inhibitory concentration |
| Residual SDs | 0 | Not reported (R2 only) |

# Part 1 - Static time-kill curves and the kill-rate model

Zhang 2019 regressed log10 CFU/mL on time over seven windows for each static
concentration and fitted the resulting kill rates against concentration.

```{r table-1}
table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~window, ~Emax, ~EC50, ~N, ~R2,
  "0-24 h", 0.09, 2.82, 1.73, 0.974,
  "0-36 h", 0.07, 1.62, 1.75, 0.970,
  "0-48 h", 0.05, 1.09, 2.53, 0.975,
  "3-24 h", 0.24, 13.04, 0.78, 0.947,
  "3-36 h", 0.09, 1.18, 1.74, 0.985,
  "3-48 h", 0.07, 0.98, 2.20, 0.985,
  "12-48 h", 0.06, 0.78, 2.98, 0.986
)
table1 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time window" = window, "Emax (1/h)" = Emax, "EC50 (ug/mL)" = EC50,
    "Hill N" = N, "R2" = R2
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Zhang 2019 Table 1. The 12-48 h row (highest R2) is packaged.")
```

```{r kill-rate-curves}
kill_rate <- function(conc, Emax, EC50, N) Emax * conc^N / (EC50^N + conc^N)
conc_grid <- 10^seq(log10(0.01), log10(8), length.out = 200)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(table1)), function(i) {
  r <- table1[i, ]
  tibble::tibble(window = r$window, conc = conc_grid,
                 kill = kill_rate(conc_grid, r$Emax, r$EC50, r$N))
}))
ggplot(curves, aes(conc, kill, colour = window, linewidth = window == "12-48 h")) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1.3, `FALSE` = 0.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Doxycycline concentration (ug/mL, log scale)",
       y = "Kill rate (log10 CFU/mL per h)", colour = "Window",
       title = "Kill rate versus concentration, all Table 1 windows",
       caption = "Zhang 2019 Table 1. The paper's figure of this relationship is not in the published article.")
```

## The ODE encoding reproduces the fitted kill rate

Holding the concentration constant (elimination switched off) recovers the static
experiment, and the decline in `log_cfu` must equal the Table 1 kill rate times
the elapsed time.

```{r static-check}
mod_kr <- readModelDb("Zhang_2019_doxycycline_killrate")
mic_mult <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 16, 32, 64)

static_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(mic_mult), function(i) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = mic_mult[i] * MIC * 300,
               cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = i, time = c(0, 12, 48), evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_,
               cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(mic_mult = mic_mult[i])
})) |>
  dplyr::filter(!(evid == 1L & amt == 0)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_static <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_kr, static_events, params = c(lkel = -60),
                  keep = "mic_mult", returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_no_omega
)

static_tab <- sim_static |>
  dplyr::group_by(mic_mult) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    ode = log_cfu[time == 48] - log_cfu[time == 12],
    conc = Cc[time == 12],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(closed = -36 * kill_rate(conc, 0.06, 0.78, 2.98))

stopifnot(max(abs(static_tab$ode - static_tab$closed)) < 1e-4)

static_tab |>
  dplyr::select(mic_mult, conc, ode, closed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Multiple of MIC" = mic_mult, "Concentration (ug/mL)" = conc,
    "ODE change 12-48 h (log10 CFU/mL)" = ode,
    "Table 1 closed form (log10 CFU/mL)" = closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Packaged ODE against the Table 1 row 12-48 h closed form at constant concentration.")
```

Against Figure 1 the 64 MIC arm fell from about 5.9 to 3.5 log10 CFU/mL between
12 and 48 h (read from the figure), a change of about -2.4 against the model's
-2.16. The low-concentration arms are less well represented: the kill-rate fit
has no growth term, so it predicts no change for the untreated control, which in
Figure 1 grew by roughly 0.85 log10 CFU/mL over the same window.

# Part 2 - Pharmacokinetics in the dynamic apparatus

The apparatus was built to reproduce oral doxycycline in pig plasma: absorption
half-life 4.15 h and elimination half-life 5.9 h (Bousquet 1998). The packaged
`ka` and `kel` are those design half-lives. The pump geometry implies nearly the
same values:

```{r geometry}
flow <- 0.58 * 60 # mL/h
geometry <- tibble::tibble(
  Constant = c("ka (1/h)", "kel (1/h)"),
  `From design half-life` = c(log(2) / 4.15, log(2) / 5.9),
  `From pump geometry` = c(flow / 210, flow / 300)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`% difference` = 100 * (`From pump geometry` / `From design half-life` - 1))
stopifnot(all(abs(geometry$`% difference`) < 2))
knitr::kable(geometry, digits = 4)
```

## Dose scaling

The paper labels its regimens in mg/kg body weight but does not state the
amount of doxycycline placed in the absorption chamber. The maintainers scaled
the regimens with a single factor, chosen so that the 10 mg/kg regimen reaches
the 1.49 ug/mL peak the paper states for it (Results, Pharmacokinetics in the in
vitro dynamic model). This is a simulation input, not a model parameter.

```{r dose-scale}
obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 96, by = 0.25), 24, 48, 72)))

dyn_events <- function(amt_ug, id) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = id, time = c(0, 24, 48), evid = 1L, amt = amt_ug,
               cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = id, time = obs_t, evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_,
               cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

unit_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_kr, dyn_events(1000, 1L), returnType = "data.frame")
ug_per_mgkg <- 1000 * 1.49 / max(unit_sim$Cc) / 10
ug_per_mgkg
```

```{r figure-4}
# Zhang 2019 Figure 4 observed points for the 10 mg/kg regimen, read from the
# figure by the maintainers (approximate).
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~conc,
  0, 0, 1, 0.40, 2, 0.69, 4, 1.01, 6, 1.20, 8, 1.15, 12, 1.02, 24, 0.26,
  30, 1.39, 36, 1.19, 48, 0.42, 54, 1.49, 60, 1.30, 72, 0.49, 84, 0.12, 96, 0.03
)
sim10 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_kr, dyn_events(10 * ug_per_mgkg, 1L),
                         returnType = "data.frame")
ggplot(sim10, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = fig4, aes(time, conc), shape = 1, colour = "red", size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, by = 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Doxycycline (ug/mL)",
       title = "10 mg/kg regimen in the dynamic apparatus",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Zhang 2019 (points read from the figure; line = packaged model).")
```

The design constants reproduce the shape of Figure 4: the first-interval peak is
`r round(max(sim10$Cc[sim10$time <= 24]), 2)` ug/mL at
`r sim10$time[which.max(sim10$Cc[sim10$time <= 24])]` h (observed 1.20 ug/mL at
6 h) and the 24 h trough is `r round(sim10$Cc[sim10$time == 24], 2)` ug/mL, close
to the 0.42 ug/mL of the paper's own WinNonlin curve (the measured point is 0.26).

```{r figure-3}
dyn_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(i) {
  dyn_events(regimens[i] * ug_per_mgkg, i) |>
    dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(paste(regimens[i], "mg/kg"),
                                   levels = paste(regimens, "mg/kg")))
}))
sim_dyn <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_kr, dyn_all, params = c(log10_cfu0 = 7.8),
                  keep = "regimen", returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = muffle_no_omega
)

ggplot(sim_dyn, aes(time, Cc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, by = 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Doxycycline (ug/mL)", colour = "Regimen",
       title = "Concentration-time curves in the dynamic apparatus",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Zhang 2019.")
```

## PKNCA on the per-interval exposures

The PK/PD indices are per dosing interval, so each 24 h interval is analysed
separately with time re-expressed after its dose.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(0:2, function(k) {
  sim_dyn |>
    dplyr::filter(time >= 24 * k, time <= 24 * (k + 1)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 24 * k, interval = k)
})) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste0(regimen, ", ", 24 * interval, "-", 24 * (interval + 1), " h")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, tad, Cc, treatment)

nca_dose <- nca_conc |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = 0, amt = 1)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ tad | treatment + id,
                             concu = "ug/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | treatment + id,
                             route = "extravascular")
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
```

The paper reports only the range of each index across all regimens and
intervals (Cmax 0.16-3.41 ug/mL, AUC24h 1.78-48.4 h*ug/mL). The maintainers
assign the lower endpoint to the first interval of the 1 mg/kg regimen and the
upper to the third interval of the 30 mg/kg regimen, the extremes in Figure 3.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "1 mg/kg, 0-24 h", 0.16, 1.78,
  "10 mg/kg, 48-72 h", 1.49, NA,
  "30 mg/kg, 48-72 h", 3.41, 48.4
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "h*ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published dynamic-apparatus exposures. * differs from reference by >20%. The 10 mg/kg Cmax is the dose-scaling anchor and matches by construction.")
```

Both ends of the range are starred, in opposite directions: the 1 mg/kg Cmax
is about 21% low and the 30 mg/kg Cmax and AUC are 31% and 54% high. The model,
which is linear, gives exactly one tenth and three times the 10 mg/kg exposure at
1 and 30 mg/kg, whereas the measured curves in Figure 3 are not
dose-proportional (the 30 mg/kg peaks are 2.3 to 2.8 times the 10 mg/kg peaks, and
the 1 mg/kg peaks are higher than one tenth of them). No linear apparatus model
can reproduce both ends of the published ranges, and the design constants were
not tuned toward either.

# Part 3 - Composing the static kill rate with the apparatus PK

The kill-rate parameters were fitted to static concentrations; the dynamic
experiment was separate. Composing them is therefore a prediction.

```{r figure-5}
ggplot(sim_dyn, aes(time, log_cfu, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, by = 12)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "M. hyopneumoniae (log10 CFU/mL)", colour = "Regimen",
       title = "Dynamic time-kill curves from the composed kill-rate model",
       caption = "Compare Figure 5 of Zhang 2019 (start set to the observed 7.8 log10 CFU/mL).")
```

```{r compose-table}
compose_tab <- sim_dyn |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(reduction = dplyr::first(log_cfu) - dplyr::last(log_cfu),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper = paper_reduction)
compose_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen,
                "Composed kill-rate model, 0-96 h (log10 CFU/mL)" = reduction,
                "Zhang 2019 reported reduction (log10 CFU/mL)" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

The composition reproduces the ordering of the regimens but under-predicts the
reduction at every one of them: by 0.4 to 0.7 log10 CFU/mL at 10 to 20 mg/kg
and by 0.8 to 1.3 log10 CFU/mL at 2.5 to 7.5 mg/kg and at 30 mg/kg. The static
fit was not built for this use: its EC50 (0.78 ug/mL) sits at or above the peak
concentrations of the 1 to 5 mg/kg regimens, so it predicts little killing there,
and its maximum of 0.06 log10 CFU/mL per hour would give at most 5.8 log10
CFU/mL over 96 h even at a constant saturating concentration, whereas the
apparatus concentration falls well below EC50 between doses. The index models in Part 4,
which were fitted to the dynamic experiment itself, track it more closely.

# Part 4 - The PK/PD index models

```{r table-2}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~index, ~e0, ~emax, ~EC50, ~N, ~R2, ~target,
  "AUC24h/MIC", -3e-05, -2.13, 179, 1.38, 0.917, 164,
  "Cmax/MIC", -5e-05, -3.14, 21, 1.01, 0.923, 9.89
)
table2 |>
  dplyr::rename("PK/PD index" = index,
                "e0 = paper 'Emax' (log10 CFU/mL)" = e0,
                "emax = paper 'E0' (log10 CFU/mL)" = emax,
                "Hill N" = N, "Published 1 log10 target" = target) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Zhang 2019 Table 2, with the paper's Emax/E0 labels mapped to the package's e0/emax.")
```

## Back-solving the published targets

The paper states that a 1 log10 reduction needs AUC24h/MIC = 164 h or
Cmax/MIC = 9.89. Solving the printed equation with the Table 2 values for
E = -1 is an independent check of the equation form and of the label mapping.

```{r backsolve}
inhib <- function(x, e0, emax, EC50, N) e0 - (e0 - emax) * x^N / (EC50^N + x^N)
backsolve <- table2 |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(solved = stats::uniroot(
    function(x) inhib(x, e0, emax, EC50, N) + 1, c(1e-3, 1e5)
  )$root) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (solved / target - 1))
stopifnot(all(abs(backsolve$pct) < 0.5))
backsolve |>
  dplyr::select(index, target, solved, pct) |>
  dplyr::rename("PK/PD index" = index, "Published target" = target,
                "Index giving exactly -1 log10" = solved, "% difference" = pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 2, 3, 2))
```

Both targets reproduce to within 0.2%. Swapping the labels back (using the
paper's Emax as the asymptote) would make the effect vanish at high exposure, so
the mapping is unambiguous.

```{r figure-6}
fig6 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(index = "AUC24h/MIC", x = seq(0, 500, length.out = 200)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(E = inhib(x, -3e-05, -2.13, 179, 1.38)),
  tibble::tibble(index = "Cmax/MIC", x = seq(0, 30, length.out = 200)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(E = inhib(x, -5e-05, -3.14, 21, 1.01))
)
ggplot(fig6, aes(x, E)) +
  geom_line(colour = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~index, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2.5, 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "PK/PD index", y = "Change over 24 h (log10 CFU/mL)",
       title = "Inhibitory sigmoid Emax fits",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6A and 6B of Zhang 2019.")
```

## The packaged ODEs reproduce the per-interval change

```{r ode-check}
mod_auc <- readModelDb("Zhang_2019_doxycycline_aucmic")
mod_cmax <- readModelDb("Zhang_2019_doxycycline_cmaxmic")

ode_check <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(0, 50, 164, 400), function(v) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_auc, data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24), evid = 0L,
                                           AUC_DOXYCYCLINE = v * MIC),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  tibble::tibble(model = "aucmic", index = v,
                 ode = s$log_cfu[2] - s$log_cfu[1],
                 closed = inhib(v, -3e-05, -2.13, 179, 1.38))
}), lapply(c(0, 5, 9.89, 25), function(v) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_cmax, data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 24), evid = 0L,
                                            CMAX_DOXYCYCLINE = v * MIC),
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  tibble::tibble(model = "cmaxmic", index = v,
                 ode = s$log_cfu[2] - s$log_cfu[1],
                 closed = inhib(v, -5e-05, -3.14, 21, 1.01))
}))
stopifnot(max(abs(ode_check$ode - ode_check$closed)) < 1e-4)
ode_check |>
  dplyr::rename("Model" = model, "Index value" = index,
                "ODE change over 24 h" = ode, "Table 2 closed form" = closed) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

## Closing the loop: apparatus PK into the index models

Feeding the per-interval AUC24h and Cmax computed by PKNCA in Part 2 into the
index models gives a predicted reduction for each regimen, summed over the three
dosing intervals.

```{r closed-loop}
loop <- nca_wide |>
  tidyr::separate(treatment, into = c("regimen", "interval"), sep = ", ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    E_auc = inhib(auclast / MIC, -3e-05, -2.13, 179, 1.38),
    E_cmax = inhib(cmax / MIC, -5e-05, -3.14, 21, 1.01)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = -sum(E_auc), cmax = -sum(E_cmax), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = paste(regimens, "mg/kg"))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(regimen) |>
  dplyr::mutate(paper = paper_reduction)

# Deterministic: a mis-transcribed index parameter or a wrong MIC moves every
# regimen at once.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(loop$auc - loop$paper)) < 0.3,
  abs(median(loop$cmax - loop$paper)) < 0.3
)

loop |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = regimen,
                "AUC24h/MIC model (log10 CFU/mL)" = auc,
                "Cmax/MIC model (log10 CFU/mL)" = cmax,
                "Zhang 2019 reported reduction (log10 CFU/mL)" = paper) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Predicted total reduction over three dosing intervals against the paper's reported reduction over the whole experiment.")
```

Both index models track the reported reductions across the dose range,
including the paper's statements that regimens above 10 mg/kg reach a
bactericidal (3 log10) reduction over the 3-day course. The comparison is
approximate: the paper's reductions cover 0-96 h whereas the index models cover
the three dosing intervals, and the dose scaling is the maintainers'.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Paper labels reversed.** Zhang 2019 calls the effect of the untreated
  control "Emax" and the maximum anti-mycoplasma effect "E0". The index models
  carry these as `e0` and `emax` respectively; the equation is unchanged in form,
  and the published 1 log10 targets reproduce to within 0.2% under this mapping.
* **Kill-rate window.** The 12-48 h row of Table 1 (highest R2, 0.986) is
  packaged. It is applied from time zero, although the window excludes the first
  12 h, in which the paper saw no marked change. The other six rows are tabulated
  above. The Results text also mentions a "maximum kill rate of 0.11/h", which
  matches no Table 1 entry; the table value is used.
* **Missing kill-rate figure.** The Results refer to "Figure 2" for the kill
  rate against concentration, but Figure 2 of the article is the apparatus
  diagram; the relationship is redrawn above from Table 1.
* **Apparatus PK.** No fitted PK parameters are printed (Figure 4 reports only
  R2 = 0.994). The packaged `ka` and `kel` are the design half-lives the
  apparatus was built to reproduce; the pump geometry agrees within 2%.
* **Dose amounts.** The amount placed in the absorption chamber for each mg/kg
  regimen is not stated. The vignette uses a single scaling factor anchored to
  the stated 1.49 ug/mL peak of the 10 mg/kg regimen; users should dose the
  killrate model in ug.
* **%T>MIC.** Figure 6C shows a %T>MIC fit (R2 = 0.823) but Table 2 gives no
  parameters for it, so it is not packaged.
* **Variability.** No between-replicate variability or residual error was
  reported; all residual SDs are 0.
* **Literature check.** No erratum or correction was found for this article
  (checked 2026-11-25).
